chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Welcome back to the next major part of the introduction to Python.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: In this bit we are going to cover functions, methods and the return value.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: To get started, let's talk about functions and methods.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Those two are very similar.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Both of them are provide useful tools.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: For example, if you have words, i.e. a string,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: a function or a method would allow you to capitalize every letter,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: or get the number of letters.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: If you have numbers, both integers and floats,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: you could for example create an absolute number,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: or select the larger of two numbers.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Also, what we have already seen, input and print are both functions.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: As a matter of fact, let's talk about those two straight in the code editor.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Here is what we finished on in the last part,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and I want to create a new Python file.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: This I do once again in the explorer.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: I want to right click, new file.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: I'm going to call this one functions underscore methods,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and don't forget dot py.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: That way we are getting a new Python file,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and with that I can work in full screen,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: so we don't have any distractions.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Let's get started with functions.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Those we have actually already seen.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: For example, print is a function,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: where we can print a value.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Also, the input statement,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: where you can ask for a value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: is also a function.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: This means that you always start with the name of a function,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then you have parentheses afterwards.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Usually you are adding a value into these parentheses,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: but that doesn't necessarily have to be the case.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: To be a bit more explicit here,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: a function always works in the same way.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: We start with a function name,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: then we have to call this function,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which we are doing with parentheses.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Into these parentheses we can add one or multiple arguments,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then the function does a certain thing.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: It could for example ask for user input,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: or it could print out a value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: or it could do a host of other things.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: After that, it can return a value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: although it doesn't necessarily have to.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: For example, input is returning a value to user input,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: but the print statement does not return a value.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And well, that is a function.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: There are quite a few inbuilt ones,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and later on we are also learning how to create our own custom functions.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And just to go over it really quickly again,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: for the print function,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we are simply printing a value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which we do with the word print,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: then we are calling parentheses,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then we are adding one or multiple values.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Same with input,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we have the word input,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: then parentheses,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then we are adding one value.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: The major difference in terms of functionality

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: of these two functions is that input returns a value.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: To demonstrate that, we can do something slightly weird.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: The input method we can wrap inside of another function,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which is going to be once again the print statement.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: What that is going to do,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: if I run the code,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we get ask for a value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and there I can write test,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then on the next line,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: this test is being printed right away.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: What essentially happened here,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: is that we start by running the input function.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: This one is going to ask for a value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then return whatever the user has entered.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: This return value is then what is being captured

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: by the print function that we have just added,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which is then what we are seeing at the end.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Via return values,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: you can chain together multiple functions easily.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: However, what you couldn't be doing,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: is to wrap this print statement,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: or rather this print statement,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: in another print statement.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: If I do that,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and print a print statement,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and run the code,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we are getting none,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: because the print statement doesn't return a value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: so Python telling us that we are well printing none,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which is what we have gotten from this line.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Can be a bit confusing in the beginning,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: but don't worry too much about it.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Just be aware that some functions return a value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: while others don't.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And let me undo the second print statement,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: because that one wouldn't make sense.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Alright, with that we have functions.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: That's literally all they do.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Besides that, we have methods.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And those are working very similar compared to functions.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: The only difference is that these are functions of data types.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Meaning that they always have to be attached to a certain kind of value.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: For example, what we could be doing.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Let's say I want to print a value that is in all lowercase letters.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: On this I can call a method,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which I do with dot,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then the method name.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And in here, vs.code gives us all of the available methods.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Strings do have quite a few.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: The one method I want to use for now is called upper.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And this also has to be called like a function,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: but it doesn't need any arguments.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: If I now comment out the stuff we have done for the functions,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and run the code again.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: We are getting value in all uppercase letters.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: That is because of this method.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: It simply looks at the string it was attached to,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then makes every letter uppercase.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: We could also create an all uppercase value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then call the method lower on it.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And once again, don't forget the parentheses.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And what this one is doing,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: is it turns every single letter into a lowercase one.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Now both of these methods aren't that useful.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: One that is a bit more interesting.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Let me add once again the word value.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And another method you could be using is called replace.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: This one, if you call it, you have to add two arguments.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: One is the letter you want to replace,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and the second argument is the letter you want to replace it with.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: For example, for this value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: I want to look for the letter e,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and replace it with the string 3.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: If I now run the code,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we are getting value, except the e at the end has become a 3.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And that is kind of all you have to know about them.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: They work exactly like a function,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: except now we are calling it with a dot,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then we have the function name,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then parentheses with arguments or without.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: We usually also get a return value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: although not necessarily.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: I suppose there is one thing you do want to be aware of.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: If I want to print 1 to 3, so an integer,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then call the upper method on it,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we would get an error,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: because integers do not have this method.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: It is only available for strings.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: No other data type has this kind of method.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: As a matter of fact, integers don't really have methods,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: at least none that are useful.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Instead, they have a couple of other functions

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: that we haven't covered yet.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Let me put it all the way at the bottom,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: other functions,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: or rather, new functions.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: For example, what you could be doing is abs,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which stands for the absolute value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which turns any number into a positive number.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Meaning if I add negative 1 in there,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: the result is going to be a 1.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: We are getting a 1,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: meaning we have turned a negative number into a positive one.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Another function you could be using that works well with numbers

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: is the max function.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: This one always picks the larger number.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: So if we have 10 and 5,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: it is going to return the 10.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: If I run the code, we are getting 10.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: That works perfectly well.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: The counterpart to the max function is the min function,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which always picks the lower value.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: If I add 0 and 1 in there,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we should be getting a 0.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Besides that, there is also a function

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: that works really well with strings.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: It is called the len function,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which is going to be much more useful later on.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: But for now, if you add a string in there,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: with let's say test,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: it is going to give you the number of characters

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: inside of the string.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: In this case, 4.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And later on, when we learn about lists and dictionaries,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: they are going to give you the items inside of this container.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: So these would be a couple of really basic functions

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: that you could be using inside of Python.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: There are loads more,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and if you are doing research online,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: you can find plenty.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: They are usually fairly straightforward to work with

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and quite accessible.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: As a matter of fact, let's do an exercise

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: where you have to do some research.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: I want you guys to create a Pythagoras theorem calculator.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: This means that once you are running the code,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: it should be asking the user for two numbers,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: the width and the height of a triangle.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And the output then is going to be the length of the hypotenuse.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: In case you have no idea what that means,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: let me explain.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: In fact, let's do all of this in Google.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: I want to look for Pythagoras theorem.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: All that Pythagoras theorem is doing is

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we are looking at a triangle with one right side,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and we are providing the length of one side,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: the length of the other side,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and the result is going to be this side.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: The formula to get this side is this one.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: We are getting the first value

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and square it, the second value and square it,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then on the resulting value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we are taking the square root.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: A really common operation,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and I'm pretty sure you are going to know it,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: but I wanted to explain it just to make sure.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: That is the kind of value I want you guys to calculate.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And there is going to be one difficulty,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and that is that the input function

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: always returns a string,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: even when a number was entered,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: meaning you have to convert a string to an integer.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: For that, you would have to do some research.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: See if you can figure it out.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Also, as a tip to simplify things a bit,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: if you want to take the square root,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: it is the same as doing the power of one half.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Pause the video now and see how far you get.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: We are in the code,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and I want to comment out all the stuff I've done so far

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: to have things a bit cleaner.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: What I want to do is

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Pythagoras theorem.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: I want to get two variables for the input.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Let's call it side a,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which I'm getting via input.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Let's call this one

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: the width of the triangle.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Don't forget the space to make the thing look a bit cleaner.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And then we also want to get side b,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which we also get via input.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And this would be the height of the triangle.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And for now, let me simply print side a

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and print side b.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: If I run the code,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we are getting the width of the triangle,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: let's say 12,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and the height of the triangle, I don't know, 4.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And we are getting 12 and 4.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And those look like numbers, but they aren't.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: To demonstrate what the problem here is,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: let me try to add a value to whatever we get from side a,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and simply add a 10 to it.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: If I now run the code again,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and add 10 and 2,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we are getting an error,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: that you can only concatenate string, not int, to a string.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Concatenate means that you are joining different strings together,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which can only be done with two strings.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: You couldn't do it with a string and an integer.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: I'll talk about this one later.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: For now, just be aware that you cannot create a sum of a string and an integer.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: So the issue is that this input is always returning a string,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: no matter what we do.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: We never get a number.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: As a consequence, we have to convert this value

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: from a string to an integer.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: How could we do that?

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Once again, for that, let's use Google.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: What you want to look for is

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: python convertStringToInt.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: As a result, we would right away get one method,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: or rather a function, called int.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And if you scroll down,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: you are getting lots of websites that talk about this.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Let's have a look at GeeksforGeeks,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: also a pretty good website.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And in there, if you scroll down,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: you get use the int function.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And then, probably a bit further down, you get an example,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: where you get actually two new functions.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: type, which gives you the type of the variable you pass into it,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and then the integer function.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: int is the one we are looking for.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: But let's play around with both, actually.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Back in our code, I want to get rid of the plus 10,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: and instead wrap site A,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: when we are printing it,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: into another function called type.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: If I now run the code again,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we once again are getting asked to provide two sites.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: I'm going to go with 10 and 10 for both.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And now for the return value.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: The first print is going to print the type of the variable

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: the user has entered,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which in this case is going to be str, short for string.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And only for the second site, so site B,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we are getting the actual value.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: Once again, understanding return value for this is really important.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: For this type print,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: we always start from the most inner part,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which in this case is site A.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: This is simply a value that we have gotten from input.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: This we are converting via the type function

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: to the type that we have gotten.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: So in this case, string.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: And after that, we are using print to print the entire value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which is this entire output bit.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: All of these are connected via the return value,

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: which is super important to understand.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: As a matter of fact, we can add one more layer to it.

chunks.title: Methods & Functions
chunks.text: We want to convert site A to an integer,
